# Raven Corps

> A community group, started in Frodsham, Cheshire, for adults who want real-world skills: map and compass, bushcraft, first aid, fitness and being ready for emergencies. Monthly meetups near Frodsham start on Saturday 23 January 2027; they are free for now. Chapters in other UK towns will follow once Frodsham is running well.

Contact: hq@ravencorps.co.uk. Sign up: https://ravencorps.co.uk/#signup

## About Raven Corps

- [About Raven Corps](https://ravencorps.co.uk/about/): Raven Corps is a community group started in Frodsham, Cheshire in 2026. It teaches adults, and later children, real-world skills in local chapters, with cadet-style ranks, a Code of seven values and a strong safeguarding policy.
- [Frequently asked questions](https://ravencorps.co.uk/faq/): Answers about Raven Corps: what it is, who can join, what it costs, what to bring, whether it's military or religious, how we keep people safe, and how to start a chapter.
- [Meetups near Frodsham](https://ravencorps.co.uk/meetups/): Raven Corps meets on the third Saturday of every month, 1pm to 3pm, near Frodsham, Cheshire. The first meetup is shelter building in Delamere Forest on Saturday 23 January 2027. Free for now, over-18s, no experience needed.
- [Skills guides](https://ravencorps.co.uk/skills/): Free, plain-English guides from Raven Corps: grid references, compass bearings, building a natural shelter, home emergency kits, storing water and the UK law on foraging.
- [Start a chapter](https://ravencorps.co.uk/start-a-chapter/): How Raven Corps chapters start: sign up and tell us your region, and when about 15 people near you have joined and someone will help lead it, we'll help you start a chapter with the curriculum, apps, brand and training.

## Skills guides

- [How to take a bearing with a compass](https://ravencorps.co.uk/skills/compass-bearing/): Line the compass edge up with your route, turn the housing to match the map's grid lines, then turn yourself until the needle sits in the arrow. A step-by-step guide to taking and walking a bearing in Britain.
- [What you can and can't forage in the UK](https://ravencorps.co.uk/skills/foraging-law/): In England and Wales you can pick wild fruit, flowers, leaves and fungi for your own use, somewhere you're allowed to be. You can't uproot wild plants without permission, pick protected species, or forage to sell without the landowner's agreement. A plain-English guide to the law and the safety rules.
- [How to read a six-figure grid reference](https://ravencorps.co.uk/skills/grid-references/): Read the easting along the bottom, then the northing up the side, and split each 1 km grid square into tenths. A step-by-step guide to six-figure grid references on Ordnance Survey maps.
- [What to put in a home emergency kit in the UK](https://ravencorps.co.uk/skills/home-emergency-kit/): The UK government's Be Ready advice is to keep three days of supplies at home: water, food, a torch, a radio, a power bank, cash, documents, medication and a first aid kit. Here's the full list, and how to keep it ready.
- [How to build a shelter from natural materials](https://ravencorps.co.uk/skills/natural-shelter/): Choose a safe spot, prop a strong ridge pole, lean sticks against it and pile on dead leaves until the layer is thick enough to keep rain and cold out. A step-by-step guide to lean-to and debris shelters in British woods.
- [How to store water for an emergency](https://ravencorps.co.uk/skills/storing-water/): Keep at least 3 litres of drinking water per person per day for three days, in sealed bottles or clean food-grade containers, somewhere cool and dark, and refresh tap-filled water regularly. How much to store, what to store it in, and how to make water safe.
